note: Research conferences and calls for abstracts that fit SafeSmoke Carbon and Carbon Clarity: clean cooking and stoves, carbon markets and climate finance, fisheries and coastal communities, gender and just transitions. Checked on the official pages; dates can change, so confirm before submitting.

items.name: International Conference on Climate Change and Just Energy Transition (I3C-JET 2027)
items.deadlineNote: Abstracts by 31 March 2027, 17:00 GMT, to i3c-jet@wascal.org. Call opened 15 November 2026.
items.fee: Africa and low/middle-income countries US$150; Master's/PhD students US$50; online US$30
items.fit: Best fit. West African, and its themes include carbon sequestration and blue/green carbon finance, economics and climate finance, low-carbon development and just energy transition, marine sciences and blue economy, and migration.
items.angle: SafeSmoke Carbon: measured fuel savings and portable benefit sharing for women fish smokers in displaced and host communities.

items.name: ETHOS 2027: the clean cookstove conference
items.deadlineNote: The listing invites submissions but gives no deadline. Check the ETHOS site now: the conference is in early February.
items.fit: ⚠️ US visas are currently suspended for South Sudanese passport holders (visa halt April 2025; full entry ban from 1 January 2026). Not possible unless the rules change or you travel on another nationality's passport. The main meeting for stove testing and cookstove carbon. Opens with 'Carbon 101' and 'Stoves 101' training on 4 February. The virtual option makes it affordable.
items.angle: Measuring kg of wood per kg of fish: a sensor protocol for commercial fish-smoking kilns.

items.name: 2027 Energy and Climate Economics and Business Days
items.deadlineNote: Abstracts or panel proposals by 15 January 2027; decisions 25 January; presenter registration by 26 February.
items.fee: €125 (both days, with meals); travel not covered
items.fit: Energy transition and climate change economics, broadly defined, including empirical work. A short abstract is enough.
items.angle: Who gets paid? Benefit-sharing design for clean-cooking carbon credits in Ghana.

items.name: EAERE 2027: European Association of Environmental and Resource Economists annual conference
items.deadlineNote: Papers, science-policy-business and thematic session proposals by 31 January 2027. Participation grant applications by 10 February 2027.
items.fit: Top environmental economics meeting. Needs a full paper, so it suits your Ghana carbon market research once written up.
items.angle: Ghana's Article 6 carbon market: who benefits? (from your research report)

items.name: SER2027: 12th World Conference on Ecological Restoration
items.deadlineNote: Abstracts (talks, lightning talks, posters) open 3 December 2026 and are due 29 January 2027.
items.fee: Not yet published; early bird from 14 January 2027
items.fit: Fits the mangrove side of SafeSmoke: fish smokers burn mangrove wood (Keta), and your community fund can pay for replanting. Has a finance and socioeconomic impact series.
items.angle: Cutting mangrove fuelwood demand through cleaner fish smoking in Ghana.

items.name: ECAS 2027: 11th European Conference on African Studies, 'African Prisms'
items.deadlineNote: The call for panels closed 27 September 2026. Papers are submitted to accepted panels; watch for the call for papers.
items.fit: Large African studies meeting with panels on environment, gender and livelihoods. Look for a panel on climate, fisheries or carbon.
items.angle: Women, smoke and carbon: fish processors and Ghana's carbon market.

items.name: Innovate4Climate 2027
items.deadlineNote: Registration details to come on the official site.
items.fit: The World Bank's flagship meeting on carbon pricing and carbon markets: buyers, developers and governments, including Article 6 deals.
items.angle: Networking: meet buyers and developers for a pilot of SafeSmoke credits.

items.name: ISEE 2027 Biennial Conference (International Society for Ecological Economics)
items.deadlineNote: Submission dates not yet published; the conference awaits final authorisation.
items.fit: Ecological economics, global South themes and just transitions.
items.angle: Fair carbon: activity rights instead of land rights for mobile women workers.

items.name: What Works Climate Solutions Summit 2027
items.deadlineNote: Abstracts closed 20 September 2026. Travel support 'under development': ask info@wwcs.science.
items.fit: Evidence on climate solutions in the global South, including food systems and health.
items.angle: Attend; plan an abstract for the next edition.

items.name: Second Summit on Clean Cooking in Africa
items.organiser: IEA, co-chaired by Kenya, Norway and the United States, with the African Union and AfDB
items.deadlineNote: The IEA says governments, institutions and companies have been invited; no public registration or call for proposals is published. Watch the IEA event page and ask partners (e.g. Clean Cooking Alliance, Ghana Energy Commission) about side events or livestream.
items.fit: The top policy and finance meeting for clean cooking in Africa (over USD 900 million in new commitments already). Directly relevant to SafeSmoke's kiln, cookstove carbon credits and finance for women processors.
items.angle: Share a one-page brief: productive-use clean cooking (fish-smoking kilns) as a missing category in Africa's clean cooking finance, with sensor-verified wood savings.

items.name: CSAE Conference 2027: Economic Development in Africa
items.organiser: Centre for the Study of African Economies, University of Oxford
items.deadlineNote: The call for papers has closed. Registration is open: speaker deadline 4 January 2027, general deadline 21 February 2027.
items.fee: Not stated on the conference page (registration via Cvent)
items.support: Limited funding for African presenters living and working in Africa (presenters only; requires a pre-conference workshop in late 2026)
items.fit: The leading meeting on African development economics; a place to meet economists working on energy, environment and markets in Ghana and West Africa. Note the 2028 call for papers for future work on Ghana's carbon market.
items.angle: For a future call: who gains from Ghana's carbon credits? Benefit-sharing rules under the Carbon Market Office and effects on women fish processors.

items.name: Conference on Advancing Africa's Industrialisation: Regional Value Chains for a Green and Resilient Future (AfCFTA Conference 2027)
items.organiser: Nelson Mandela School of Public Governance, University of Cape Town
items.deadlineNote: Full papers, policy briefs, case studies or panel proposals by 31 January 2027. Contact: mapoulo.ntoane@uct.ac.za.
items.fit: African green industrialisation, climate finance and a 'Towards COP32' session. SafeSmoke is a green value-chain upgrade for fish processing, a strong policy-brief angle.
items.angle: Greening Africa's fish value chain: cleaner kilns, measured fuel savings and carbon income for women processors (policy brief or case study).

items.name: EGU General Assembly 2027 (European Geosciences Union)
items.deadlineNote: The call for abstracts is open; check the exact abstract and financial-support deadlines on the EGU27 'Deadlines and milestones' page. Session ERE0.1 'Bridging the gap between climate risk and energy access' fits SafeSmoke.
items.fee: Not stated here; EGU offers fee waivers and financial support (check eligibility)
items.support: Financial support and waivers (check the EGU27 page)
items.fit: Huge hybrid meeting with an online option. The energy-access and climate-risk session matches clean fish-smoking energy and measured savings.
items.angle: Measuring energy access at the kiln: sensor evidence of fuel savings in Ghana's fish smoking.

items.name: Environmental Markets Conference 2027
items.organiser: Alliance for Environmental Markets and Investments (AEMI)
items.deadlineNote: The main call has closed; digital presentations and posters are open until 5 March 2027.
items.support: Financial assistance and awards page (check eligibility)
items.fit: ⚠️ US visas are currently suspended for South Sudanese passport holders (visa halt April 2025; full entry ban from 1 January 2026). Not possible unless the rules change or you travel on another nationality's passport. Has a 'Carbon Markets & Climate Solutions' track covering MRV, voluntary markets and climate finance. Good for networking with credit buyers, but travel to the USA is costly.
items.angle: Poster: digital MRV and fair benefit sharing for small-scale clean-cooking credits in Ghana.

items.name: 2027 AERE Summer Conference (Association of Environmental and Resource Economists)
items.deadlineNote: Abstract submissions open 1 December 2026 and close in early to mid-January 2027 (exact date to be announced). Registration opens mid-March.
items.fee: Not stated; reduced fees for AERE members
items.support: Not stated; graduate-student programming (ask info@aere.org about grants)
items.fit: ⚠️ US visas are currently suspended for South Sudanese passport holders (visa halt April 2025; full entry ban from 1 January 2026). Not possible unless the rules change or you travel on another nationality's passport. The main US environmental economics meeting: carbon markets, energy, development and environment. Good for your Ghana carbon market research and SafeSmoke's benefit-sharing design.
items.angle: Who benefits from clean-cooking carbon credits? Evidence and benefit-sharing design from Ghana's fish-smoking sector.

items.name: RGS-IBG Annual International Conference 2027 (Royal Geographical Society)
items.city: UK (usually London, late Aug/early Sep; dates to be announced)
items.mode: In person, online or hybrid (depends on session)
items.deadlineNote: Submit a paper or poster by Fri 19 Feb 2027 via the Ex Ordo portal (opens by end of Nov 2026). Best route: answer a session call from the Development Geographies or energy research groups. Presenters register and pay by 18 Jun 2027.
items.fee: Conference fee (amount on the RGS site); reduced rates usually for students and low-income countries
items.support: Check research-group bursaries for postgraduates and Global South presenters
items.fit: UK: South Sudanese passport holders need a UK Standard Visitor visa (apply online, biometrics at the visa centre in Accra). Apply as soon as you're accepted. Online presentation is possible in many sessions, so you can present without a visa. Big geography meeting with strong development, energy and climate-justice sessions. Good fit for SafeSmoke's benefit-sharing and inclusion work.
items.angle: Who gets paid when smoke becomes carbon? Women fish processors, benefit sharing and Ghana's carbon market.

items.name: All-Energy 2027 (call for speakers)
items.deadlineNote: Speaker abstracts close 21 Dec 2026 (one per topic). Best theatres: Heat & Community Energy (energy poverty, community ownership) and Innovation (AI, data, start-ups).
items.fee: Not stated (exhibition is usually free to attend)
items.fit: UK: South Sudanese passport holders need a UK Standard Visitor visa (apply online, biometrics at the visa centre in Accra). Apply as soon as you're accepted. The UK's largest renewable energy event, aimed at industry. A good stage for SafeSmoke as an innovation (sensors and dMRV) but less academic. Speakers are usually expected in person.
items.angle: Measuring clean cooking with IoT: from fish-smoking kilns in Accra to audit-ready carbon data.

items.name: BIEE Research Conference 2027 (British Institute of Energy Economics)
items.deadlineNote: Call not out yet. BIEE normally opens abstracts early in the year with a spring deadline. Check biee.org from February.
items.support: Student and early-career prizes are usual; ask about bursaries
items.fit: UK: South Sudanese passport holders need a UK Standard Visitor visa (apply online, biometrics at the visa centre in Accra). Apply as soon as you're accepted. The UK's main academic energy-economics meeting. Strong fit for Ghana's carbon market (Article 6, carbon pricing) and clean-cooking economics.
items.angle: Article 6 and clean cooking in Ghana: who captures the value of carbon credits?

items.name: Development Studies Association Conference 2027 (DSA2027)
items.organiser: DSA, University of Sussex and Institute of Development Studies
items.deadlineNote: The call for panels has closed; the call for papers into those panels usually follows in early 2027. Watch devstud.org.uk.
items.fee: Not stated; reduced rates usually for Global South participants
items.support: DSA usually runs a call for funding for Global South and early-career presenters
items.fit: UK: South Sudanese passport holders need a UK Standard Visitor visa (apply online, biometrics at the visa centre in Accra). Apply as soon as you're accepted. Hybrid, so you can present online without a visa. The UK's main development conference, co-hosted by IDS, with very strong interest in inclusion, displacement and just transitions. Excellent fit for the challenge themes.
items.angle: Carbon literacy for displaced and host communities: designing fair benefit sharing in West African clean-cooking projects.

items.name: Canada–Africa Academic Collaborations Conference (CAACC2027)
items.deadlineNote: The page lists both 6 Nov and 25 Nov 2026 as the deadline, so it has probably just closed. Email africain@uwo.ca today to ask whether late abstracts are accepted. There is a separate Emerging Scholars invitation.
items.fit: No visa needed (online and free). Track 2 (health, wellbeing and sustainable development) and Track 3 (technology and innovation) fit SafeSmoke well. A good way to meet Canadian partners for later study.
items.angle: Co-creating carbon literacy tools with women fish processors in Ghana: an Africa–Canada partnership opportunity.

items.name: Toronto Meeting on the Economics of Climate Change (TMEC 2027)
items.deadlineNote: Submissions are not open yet. Check tmec.ca from January.
items.fit: Canada: you need a Canadian visitor visa (apply online with IRCC, biometrics at the VFS centre in Accra). Processing can take months, so apply as soon as you're accepted. A focused climate-economics research meeting. Best with a more developed paper (for example, carbon market design or clean-cooking evidence).
items.angle: Carbon credit benefit sharing and household welfare: evidence from Ghana's fish-smoking sector.

items.name: Canadian Economics Association 61st Annual Meetings (CEA 2027)
items.deadlineNote: Deadline not posted yet; it is usually mid-February. The presenter needs CEA membership.
items.fee: CEA membership plus registration (student rates available)
items.fit: Canada: you need a Canadian visitor visa (apply online with IRCC, biometrics at the VFS centre in Accra). Processing can take months, so apply as soon as you're accepted. Large economics meeting with environment, resource and development sessions; the CREEA environmental economists also take part.
items.angle: Do carbon payments reach women? Mobile-money benefit sharing in Ghana's clean-cooking projects.

items.organiser: Federation for the Humanities and Social Sciences; CASID
items.city: Simon Fraser University, Vancouver (virtual 18–21 May; in person 5–9 Jul)
items.deadlineNote: CASID's 2027 call isn't out yet. In 2026 the deadline was 13 January, so expect a similar date. Watch casid-acedi.ca.

Congress has a virtual week (18–21 May), so you may be able to present online. CASID is Canada's development studies association: strong fit for inclusion and benefit sharing.
items.angle: Inclusion strategies for displaced and host communities in carbon projects: lessons from Ghana.

items.name: CREEA 2027 (Canadian Resource and Environmental Economics Association)
items.city: Canada (host to be announced; usually early October)
items.deadlineNote: Usually opens in summer with an early-August deadline (2026: 5 Aug). Short extended abstracts are accepted.
items.fit: Canada: you need a Canadian visitor visa (apply online with IRCC, biometrics at the VFS centre in Accra). Processing can take months, so apply as soon as you're accepted. Small, friendly environmental-economics meeting that takes early-stage work as short talks.
items.angle: Measuring fuel savings for carbon credits: kiln sensor data from Accra.

items.name: 35th IAFFE Annual Conference: Inequalities, Power Structures, and Transnational Solidarities
items.organiser: International Association for Feminist Economics, with JAFFE and Okayama University
items.deadlineNote: Abstracts and travel grants closed 16 November 2026. Registration opens 18 January 2027; fees are not yet published. The online segment (17–18 June) avoids travel costs.
items.fee: Not yet published; IAFFE members get discounts
items.support: Travel grants (priority for Global South and early-career scholars) closed 16 Nov 2026; watch for the 2028 round
items.fit: Japan: a visa is needed, so apply early through the Embassy of Japan in Accra if attending in person. The main feminist economics meeting, with an online segment. Fits women-first benefit sharing and the value of women's work in fish processing.
items.angle: For 2028: paying women for the carbon they save. Benefit-sharing design for women fish processors in Ghana's carbon market.
